name: Guyana

legalStatuses.label: Registered business name
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: One source gives about G$5,000. Confirm the current fee with DCRA.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: Incorporation fees are higher than for a business name. Confirm the current fees with DCRA.

launchSteps.label: Get your TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number) from GRA
launchSteps.plain: A number that identifies you to the tax office. You need it for almost every other step.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: If you trade under any name other than your own, you must register it under the Business Names (Registration) Act. Search the name at DCRA first.

launchSteps.label: Register the business name, or incorporate the company, at DCRA
launchSteps.plain: You file the form and pay the fee at the DCRA office. A company must also meet the Companies Act requirements.

launchSteps.label: Register with GRA and plan your advance tax payments
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people pay income tax in advance, each quarter, and file a yearly return by April 30.

launchSteps.label: Register with the National Insurance Scheme (NIS)
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people must register and contribute. It gives access to a pension and other benefits.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer and prepare monthly payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay income tax (PAYE) and NIS each month, by the 15th of the following month.

launchSteps.label: Register for VAT
launchSteps.plain: Required when your yearly sales reach G$15,000,000. Apply to the GRA VAT department.

incomeTax.label: Income tax
incomeTax.allowanceNote: G$1,680,000 a year, or one third of your profit if that is more
incomeTax.bracketText: 25% on chargeable income up to G$3,360,000, then 35%

corporateTax.label: Corporation tax
corporateTax.note: 40% is the rate for commercial companies (trade, manufacturing). Other companies pay 25%. Confirm which applies to you with GRA.

contributions.label: NIS
contributions.plain: National Insurance Scheme. It gives access to a pension and other benefits. Self-employed people pay 12.5% of their declared income, up to G$280,000 a month.

vat.label: Value Added Tax
vat.registerNote: Apply to the GRA VAT department.
vat.filingNote: VAT returns are due within 21 days after each period.

calendar.quarterlyTextPersonal: Pay your advance income tax instalment.
calendar.quarterlyTextCorporate: Pay your advance corporation tax instalment.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File your income tax return for the year before.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay income tax (PAYE) and NIS for the previous month.
calendar.vatText: If registered for VAT: file your return within 21 days after each period.

notes: Optional deductions (for children, or for medical and life insurance premiums) are not included in your estimate. They would lower your tax.
